verses.text: Some time later, Joseph was told, “Your father is sick.” So he took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and went to see him. 🏥
When Jacob heard, “Your son Joseph has come,” Israel gathered his strength and sat up on the bed. He wanted to meet him properly. 💛
Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in Canaan and blessed me.” He remembered the promise. ✨

“God told me, ‘I’ll make you fruitful and multiply your family into a community of peoples. I’ll give this land to your descendants as a lasting possession.’” The promise reached beyond one generation. 🌱

“Now your two sons born to you in Egypt before I came here will be mine: Ephraim and Manasseh will count as my own, just like Reuben and Simeon.” Jacob formally welcomed them into the family line. 👨‍👦
“Any children you have after them will be yours, but they’ll be counted under their brothers’ names for their inheritance.” Jacob explained how the family line would be shared. 📜

“As for me, Rachel died beside me in Canaan while we were traveling from Paddan, still some distance from Ephrath. I buried her there on the road to Ephrath—now called Bethlehem.” Jacob remembered her. 🕯️
Israel noticed Joseph’s sons and asked, “Who are these?” 👀
Joseph answered his father, “These are the sons God gave me here.” Israel said, “Bring them to me, please, so I can bless them.” 🙏
Israel’s eyesight had grown dim with age. Joseph brought the boys close, and their grandfather kissed and hugged them. 🫂
Israel said to Joseph, “I never expected to see your face again, and now God has even let me see your children.” His joy overflowed. 🥹
Joseph moved the boys away from between his knees and bowed with his face to the ground. 🙇
He took them both: Ephraim in his right hand, toward Israel’s left, and Manasseh in his left, toward Israel’s right. Then he brought them close. 🤲
Israel crossed his hands, placing his right hand on Ephraim, the younger, and his left on Manasseh. He did it knowingly, even though Manasseh was the firstborn. ✋
Then Jacob blessed Joseph: “The God my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked with—the God who has cared for me all my life to this day—” 🙏
“the angel who rescued me from every evil—may he bless these boys. May my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac live on through them. May they grow into a multitude across the earth.” 🌍
Joseph saw his father’s right hand resting on Ephraim’s head, and it bothered him. He lifted his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim to Manasseh. ✋
Joseph said, “Not that way, father. Manasseh is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.” 🗣️

His father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. Manasseh will become a people, and he too will be great. But his younger brother will become greater, and his descendants will grow into many nations.” 🔮
That day Jacob blessed them, saying, “Israel will use your names in a blessing: ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’” He placed Ephraim ahead of Manasseh. 🙏
Israel said to Joseph, “I’m about to die, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.” 🕊️
“And I’m giving you one portion more than your brothers—the land I took from the Amorites with my sword and bow.” Jacob made his gift clear. 🏹
